name: glucose-regulation
title: Glucose Regulation — COPASI vs Tellurium
question:
Do COPASI and Tellurium agree on the dynamics of BioModels matching
"glucose regulation"?

study_card.goal: Fetch glucose-regulation BioModels and score COPASI-vs-Tellurium agreement.
study_card.mechanism: search_biomodels(query) -> pbg-biomodels compare (LoadBiomodelStep + per-engine UTC + all-pairs nRMSE).
study_card.expected_result: Most models agree closely; divergences/load-failures are flagged per model.
study_card.main_expert_question: Are divergent models real dynamics differences or engine loading artifacts?

biological_summary:
Hepatic and pancreatic glucose-regulation models (Bulik2016 hepatic glucose
metabolism, Sturis/Tolic insulin-glucose ultradian oscillators, Topp/Silber
beta-cell mass models) are stiff ODE systems spanning enzymatic and
hormonal timescales. Running the same SBML under two independent
numerical engines (COPASI's LSODA-based integrator vs Tellurium's
libRoadRunner/CVODE) is a cross-engine correctness check: close agreement
means the dynamics are numerically robust to the solver, not an artifact
of one engine's defaults; disagreement or a load failure flags either a
genuinely stiff/edge-case model or an engine-specific SBML-loading gap
(e.g. no SED-ML present to fix a simulation protocol).

report.title: Glucose Regulation — 1/5 models loaded in both engines, agreement 'Good' (nRMSE 2.05e-7); 4/5 fail on missing SED-ML
report.objective:
Do COPASI and Tellurium agree on the dynamics of BioModels matching
"glucose regulation"?
report.conclusion:
A live run (`run_glucose_regulation(max_results=5)`) against the top 5
"glucose regulation" BioModels search hits loaded only 1/5
(BIOMD0000000633, Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism) successfully
under both COPASI and Tellurium: 30 shared species, mean nRMSE
2.05e-07, bucket "Good (<=1%)" — near-perfect cross-engine agreement.
This matches the committed full-corpus comparison dataset's independent
measurement for the same model (auto_ten_seconds job: mean nRMSE
1.61e-07, also "good"), cross-validating both runs. The other 4/5
(MODEL2001080002, MODEL1112110004, MODEL1806080001, MODEL2005050001 —
all non-curated `MODEL*` BioModels preprint entries, not `BIOMD*`
curated models) failed identically with
`ValueError: could not find a .sedml file in entry` — a load-time
gap (no SED-ML simulation protocol packaged with the entry), not a
numerical-agreement failure.
report.caveat:
Small sample (5 models, capped for run time); the 80% load-failure rate
is driven entirely by non-curated `MODEL*` search hits lacking SED-ML,
not by curated `BIOMD*` models — a `curated_only` filter (as used by the
full-corpus catalog, Task A) would likely raise the load-success rate.
Only one model actually exercised the COPASI-vs-Tellurium agreement
comparison this run; broader agreement-bucket statistics come from the
committed corpus dataset (`glucose-biomodel-do`/`corpus-coverage`
studies), not this study's own baseline scope.

findings.statement:
The one curated model that loaded in both engines (BIOMD0000000633,
Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism) shows near-perfect cross-engine
agreement (mean nRMSE 2.05e-07, bucket "Good"), independently
cross-validated by the committed full-corpus dataset's measurement of
the same model (1.61e-07, also "good") -- confirming COPASI and
Tellurium integrate this stiff hepatic-glucose ODE system to
numerically indistinguishable trajectories. The other 4/5 models fail
identically on a missing SED-ML file, a load-time gap rather than a
numerical disagreement.

evidence.summary: mean nRMSE 2.05e-07 (this run) vs 1.61e-07 (committed corpus dataset), both bucket 'Good (<=1%)', for BIOMD0000000633 across 30 shared species; 4/5 other models fail with 'could not find a .sedml file'.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline composite run (live 5-model fetch + COPASI/Tellurium compare) completed end-to-end without error.

biological_validation.basis: The one model that loaded in both engines agrees to nRMSE 2.05e-07 (bucket 'Good'), cross-validated by an independent 1.61e-07 measurement on the committed corpus dataset -- genuine cross-engine numerical agreement on real dynamics, not calibrated against experimental data.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 reframes the 80% load-failure rate as a load-time SED-ML gap (non-curated MODEL* entries), not a genuine engine disagreement -- the study's central interpretive claim.

limitations: Only 1/5 models in this run's 5-model sample loaded in both engines; the study's own agreement statistic (n=1) is too small to generalize -- broader nRMSE-bucket statistics come from the separately-committed full-corpus dataset, not this study's baseline run.
The load-failure diagnosis (missing SED-ML) is inferred from an identical exception message across all 4 failures, not independently verified per model.

resolved_uncertainties: Divergence in this query is driven by non-curated MODEL* entries lacking SED-ML, not by genuine COPASI/Tellurium numerical disagreement.
remaining_uncertainties: Why do most curated glucose models fail to load in both engines (missing SED-ML)? Can they be recovered?
Which models, if any, genuinely disagree in dynamics vs merely fail to load?

followup_study_proposals.title: Multi-organ glucose homeostasis (M4/Herrgardh)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Import the M4/Herrgardh multi-organ glucose homeostasis model for a coupled multi-organ Aim-2 demonstration, moving beyond single-organ SBML comparison.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: Wire the M4/Herrgardh multi-organ (liver-pancreas-periphery) glucose model into a viva-human-atlas composite and run it as a coupled demo, comparing organ-level fluxes against the single-organ models already catalogued here.

followup_study_proposals.title: Load-failure recovery (auto-generate default SED-ML)
followup_study_proposals.motivation: Auto-generate a default UTC/SED-ML simulation protocol for BioModels entries missing one, to recover the 4/5 models this study's own run could not load in either engine.
followup_study_proposals.proposed_experiment: For each MODEL* entry that fails with 'could not find a .sedml file', auto-generate a minimal uniform-time-course SED-ML wrapper (default duration/steps inferred from the SBML's own units) and re-attempt the COPASI/Tellurium load+compare.

assumptions: SBML semantics are engine-agnostic: a curated SBML file defines one mathematical model, so COPASI and Tellurium integrating it should converge to the same trajectory up to solver tolerance -- any large divergence is a model/engine artifact, not biology.
A BioModels entry without a packaged SED-ML simulation protocol cannot be auto-run and fails at LOAD time, independent of the numerical engine -- distinct from a solver-level numerical disagreement.
nRMSE over the shared species is a meaningful cross-engine agreement metric, and pbg-biomodels' pre-stated 'Good (<=1%)' bucket boundary is a reasonable agreement threshold.
The 'glucose regulation' top-5 query over COPASI + Tellurium is a representative but small sample; the single model that loaded in both engines is not a population-level agreement statistic.

literature_anchors.expectation: COPASI integrates SBML via its LSODA-based deterministic solver, the reference engine this study checks Tellurium against.
literature_anchors.source: Hoops et al. 2006 -- supports COPASI as an established SBML ODE integrator.

literature_anchors.expectation: Tellurium's libRoadRunner (CVODE) is an independent high-performance SBML integrator, so agreement with COPASI is a genuine cross-implementation check, not two runs of the same solver.
literature_anchors.source: Somogyi et al. 2015 -- supports libRoadRunner as an independent SBML integration engine.

literature_anchors.expectation: Curated BIOMD* BioModels entries are the SED-ML-complete, trustworthy subset; non-curated MODEL* preprint entries may ship without a simulation protocol and fail to load.

literature_anchors.source: Malik-Sheriff et al. 2020 -- supports the curated-vs-non-curated BioModels distinction behind the load failures.

alternative_hypotheses.claim:
The apparent 4/5 "disagreement" in this query is numerical: COPASI and
Tellurium diverge on these stiff glucose-regulation models (different
integrators / default tolerances), so the models genuinely fail to agree.
alternative_hypotheses.discriminated_by:
All 4 non-loading models fail BEFORE any integration, with the identical
exception "could not find a .sedml file in entry" -- a load-time SED-ML
gap, raised before the solver runs, not a per-species nRMSE divergence.
The one model that does load (BIOMD0000000633) agrees to mean nRMSE
2.05e-07. So the failures are load-time, not solver-level divergence.
evidence_against: Identical 'could not find a .sedml file in entry' exception across all 4/5 failures -- a load-path error raised before the solver runs.
The one model that loads agrees near-perfectly (mean nRMSE 2.05e-07, bucket 'Good'), cross-validated at 1.61e-07 by the committed corpus dataset.
